purpose: A run of children with one gap between them — the default way to space anything inside a page.

useInstead.when: the children are peers that should reflow into columns
useInstead.use: Grid — is this a sequence, or a set?

useInstead.when: the content needs a visible surface

decision.authority: This guard is the authority for Stack decisions in this package.
decision.beforeTheRules: Stack exists so spacing is not something a caller can forget. <main> spaces its own direct children, but that reach stops one level down — the moment anything is wrapped in a plain div, the rhythm inside is whatever the markup happened to do.

rules.if: the children read top to bottom
rules.because: it is the default and the common case

rules.if: the children sit side by side — a toolbar, a label and its control
rules.because: it also centres them vertically and wraps by default, so a narrow viewport does not overflow

rules.if: the children are separate blocks of page content
rules.because: it defaults to the same 16px as <main> and Grid, which is what makes the page read as one rhythm

rules.if: the children are tightly related — a heading and its subtitle
rules.then: step DOWN the scale, gap="spacing.1" or "spacing.2"
rules.because: closeness is how the layout says two things belong together; that is the same reason Card's inner gap is 8px

rules.if: you need something pushed to the far end — actions against a title
rules.then: use justify="between" on a horizontal Stack
rules.because: it beats a spacer element or margin-left: auto, both of which stop working when a child is removed

constraints: Stack sets no margins on its children. Spacing is the gap, always.
min-width is 0, so a long unbroken string in one child cannot force the row wider than its container.

defaults.wrap: true for horizontal, false for vertical

composition.childrenContract: Anything. Each child is a flex item with the gap between it and the next.
composition.notes: Nesting Stacks is normal and correct — an outer one at 16px with an inner one at 4px is how a heading group sits inside a page.

antiPatterns.dont: Adding margin-bottom to children to space them
antiPatterns.why: the last child gets a trailing margin nothing needs, and the value drifts wherever someone forgets

antiPatterns.dont: Wrapping content in a plain <div> for layout inside a page
antiPatterns.why: a bare div has no gap, so spacing inside it becomes whatever the markup happened to do

antiPatterns.dont: Using an empty element as a spacer
antiPatterns.do: Change the gap, or use justify="between"
antiPatterns.why: a spacer is invisible state that breaks the moment the layout changes

antiPatterns.do: Pass a token from the spacing scale
antiPatterns.why: a raw value escapes the rhythm and that one group stops matching the page

incorrect.why: a bare div plus margins — use a Stack and let the gap space them
the spacer div is doing what justify="between" does declaratively
